content:
Since the only two-digit palindrome prime is \(11\), any valid year must be \(11\) times a three-digit palindrome prime.

For \(1001\), \(1001=7\cdot 11\cdot 13\), but \(1001/11=91\), which is not three-digit, so \(1001\) does not qualify.

Check the palindromic years:
\[
1001,1111,1221,1331,1441,1551,1661,1771,1881,1991
\]
Divide each by \(11\):
\[
91,101,111,121,131,141,151,161,171,181
\]
The three-digit palindrome primes among these are:
\[
101,131,151,181
\]
Thus the valid years are:
\[
1111,1441,1661,1991
\]
There are \(4\) such years.

\boxed{4}
